@@137405113 <p> A sweeping internal review of the Democrats ' 2024 election losses runs nearly 200 pages . The autopsy report , released on Thursday after months of speculation and delay , was meant to capture why and how the Democrats lost the White House and collapsed electorally nationwide . <p> Along with a slew of mistakes , it contains some damning findings that examine spending patterns , media strategy , voter contact and organizing failures across the ballot , describing a party that has lost ground at every level of government for nearly two decades . <p> But the report also manages to avoid almost every question the party 's voters are actually asking about the consequential decisions of the cycle . <h> 1 . What 's not in it : Joe Biden staying in the race for as long as he did <p> The decision by Biden -- and the party apparatus around him -- to seek re-election despite evident cognitive decline and alarm over his old age , and the months following in which donors , elected officials and senior Democrats privately acknowledged concerns they refused to raise @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ became the Democratic nominee without a single primary vote being cast in her favor . <p> While switching Harris in was credited in the report with boosting down-ballot Democrats , the candidate anointment is treated as an event that happened to the party rather than a crisis the party created and then managed badly . <h> 2 . What 's not in it : Gaza , at all <p> Your control+F is not broken : in the nearly 200 pages of reporting , the words " Gaza " and " Israel " do not appear . <p> During the Michigan primary in 2024 , the " uncommitted " protest movement drew more than 100,000 votes in a state Biden had won by about 154,000 in 2020 , and Harris would lose by about 100,000 . <p> After the election loss , one poll from YouGov/IMEU Policy Project found the top concern nationally for 2020 Biden voters who did n't go for Harris in 2024 was " ending Israel 's violence in Gaza " . Under the party 's own traditional budget frameworks , voter contact spending should have been closer to $300m . <p> The gap , the report suggests , reflected an outdated " strategy of scarcity " that no longer made sense given the amount of money available . <h> 6 . They learned about them , in some cases , by reading the press . <h> 7 . What 's in it : annotations <p> One notable feature of the report is that it is filled with annotations about the claims contained in the report . <p> At the top of each page , a red disclaimer reads : " This document reflects the views of the author , not the DNC . The DNC was not provided with the underlying sourcing , interviews or supporting data for many of the assertions contained herein and therefore can not independently verify the claims presented . " <p> Elsewhere in the document , annotations raise concerns about the accuracy of the findings . What 's in it : the male voter collapse was solvable <p> North Carolina 's governor , Josh Stein , won 51% of male voters in the same election in which Harris won just 40% . In @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ a secular stand-in for the Virgin Mary , as well as representing the loss of what she once meant to our culture spiritually . <p> The development of Marian doctrine and her deep theological significance was a gradual process over many centuries . Crucially , it was believed that Mary could spiritually intercede on humanity 's behalf and provide vital support throughout the storms of life , especially in matters concerning our eternal salvation . <p> The Queen of Heaven reigned supreme , subordinate only to the Trinity , right up until the Reformational wreckage of the 16th century , during which , in many European countries , she was abruptly dethroned . These figures , once revered and romanticised , had , to some extent , been usurped by the advent of Hollywood and industrialised entertainment . As such , a new roster of " stars " was born , further diverting our attention away from religion and the spiritual life . <p> From Clara Bow to Marilyn Monroe , these idols were marketed to women in particular . While the Catholicism of the Middle Ages made it paramount that Mary pointed to Christ , these new figures , much like contemporary pop singers , were gateways to beauty ideals , glamour and aspirational lifestyles . But they were never a bridge to motherhood . @@137459692 <p> America 's Middle East by Marc Lynch is a book written against amnesia , and against the greasy consolations by which empires survive their crimes . <p> It is also , improbably , a magnificent act of civic faith . Lynch begins in rage , but he does not remain there . <p> The anger that animates these pages is not the ornamental fury of the columnist or the safely retrospective indignation of the memoirist . <p> It is the rage of someone who has lived inside the institutions through which American Middle East policy is made , and who has finally concluded that the machine did not merely malfunction . It worked as designed . <p> Lynch is unusually well placed to make the case . A professor at George Washington University 's Elliott School , he is one of the most important American interpreters of Arab politics of recent decades . <h> New MEE newsletter : Jerusalem Dispatch <h> Sign up to get the latest insights and analysis on Israel-Palestine , alongside Turkey Unpacked and other MEE newsletters <p> He has written on the Arab public sphere @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ . Lynch is not a parachutist , nor a late convert discovering Palestine after scrolling through horrors on a phone . <p> His work has long moved between scholarship and policy , between the public hopes of the region and the bureaucratic habits of the power that has so often crushed them . <p> That double vision gives the book its force . Lynch knows the American policy world too intimately to caricature it , and the Middle East too seriously to forgive it . <h> Establishing a brutal order <p> The argument is sweeping and patient . Since 1991 , the United States has not merely entered the region . It has constituted a regional order : America 's Middle East . <p> That order rests on military primacy , protection of Israel , the arming and preservation of autocratic allies , containment of Iran , the policing of permissible politics , and the routine conversion of Arab and Muslim suffering into strategic background noise . <p> It promised peace , democracy , development and stability . It produced Iraq 's ruin , a frozen and fraudulent peace process @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ Libya 's collapse , Syria 's inferno , Yemen 's starvation , Sudan 's abandonment and genocide in Gaza . <p> Palestine is the book 's moral centre , even when Lynch widens the lens beyond it . <p> His argument is not simply that Washington failed to broker a just settlement , but that the so-called peace process became one of the central institutions of American regional domination . It converted occupation into process , dispossession into negotiation , and Palestinian political existence into a security problem to be managed . <p> The Oslo accords appear here not as a lost opportunity tragically squandered , but as a structure that allowed Israel to deepen control while the United States preserved the fiction of mediation . <p> Gaza , in this reading , is not an aberration . It is the endpoint of a system that treated Palestinian life as administratively inconvenient and Palestinian resistance as proof of unfitness for freedom . <p> Lynch is especially sharp on the way American policy makes Palestinian suffering visible only when it threatens regional order , never when it demands justice . <p> @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ Saudi , Emirati , Egyptian , Israeli , Iranian , Syrian and other actors appear here as agents with projects , cruelties and calculations of their own . <p> But Lynch rejects the alibi of local agency when it becomes a way of laundering American responsibility . <p> Washington did not invent every despot , militia or war . It did , however , build the weather in which they learned to move . It rewarded brutality , sanctioned others , excused allies , demonised enemies , disciplined knowledge and then called the resulting wasteland order . <h> Different leadership , same destructive mindset <p> There is a grim comedy in the continuity Lynch describes . Presidents arrive promising to pivot , rebalance , end forever wars or make a new beginning . <p> They leave having reproduced the same architecture . George HW Bush launches the order from the wreckage of Iraq . <p> Bill Clinton sanctifies it through sanctions and Oslo 's theatrical promise . George W Bush breaks it by invading Iraq , while claiming to democratise the region by force . <p> Barack Obama sees more @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ American footprint , reaches for the Iran nuclear deal , then is pulled back by inherited compulsions . <p> Donald Trump strips the system of liberal pretence , embraces transactional cruelty and normalisation without Palestine . <p> Joe Biden , the institutionalist , brings the edifice to its moral nadir by arming and shielding Israel as Gaza is pulverised . <h> Nuanced approaches <p> Lynch 's treatment of Islamism is one of the book 's quieter strengths . He refuses the lazy American habit of treating Islamists as a single civilisational threat , forever outside politics , history and social life . <p> Islamism in these pages is neither romanticised nor flattened . Hamas , the Muslim Brotherhood , Hezbollah , the Houthis and other Islamist actors are placed inside specific political orders , wars , occupations , state collapses and fields of repression . <p> Lynch understands that movements formed under occupation , dictatorship or foreign assault can not be explained by theology alone . <p> At the same time , he does not turn them into noble vessels of resistance . They have their own hierarchies , coercions @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ is that the American order has repeatedly helped produce the very Islamist forces it later claims to be fighting , whether by closing non-violent political routes , backing dictators who crush elected Islamists , tolerating occupation , or reducing whole societies to security laboratories . <p> Anti-Islamism becomes , in Washington and among its Arab allies , a grammar of rule . It justifies prisons , coups , surveillance , bombing and the permanent suspicion of popular politics . <h> Designed to fail <p> The most disturbing claim in the book is not that American policy failed . Failure would be a softer word , suggesting error , miscalculation , tragedy . <p> Lynch 's harsher point is that many of these policies succeeded according to their own metrics . <p> American centrality was reaffirmed in every crisis , even when that centrality made resolution impossible . <p> The scandal is not only that Arabs and Muslims are dehumanised . It does not need to be . It is only the first claim I have a problem with , but it 's a problem that cascades through the theoretical system of the book . Kant , after all , argued that " world peace is enhanced by the spread of trade and investment ... " <p> The second , related , problem is that Hamilton then has to flatten geopolitics in order to make the various blocs fit within his scheme . The European Union is presented as Kantian , as universalist , as good . Against this , we are told that the Chinese elite , including Xi Jinping , has become smitten with Schmitt and therefore takes up the position of bad . The COPs are a battle between good and bad , and bad is winning . <p> The evidence of Schmitt 's influence on elite thinking in China is alarming and revealing . The idea that China would move further from any kind of socialism and towards a modern National Socialism @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ Chinese government . But Hamilton goes too far , exhibiting only what can be described as Schmittian Sinophobia . He describes China 's " chronic anxiety and paranoia " and claims that " under Xi Jinping 's rule , China has increasingly taken on the characteristics of a fascist state " and aims to build " a new Sinocentric world order " . <p> Stockpiles <p> Hamilton 's central claim - that Schmitt is gaining influence and this undermines climate action - is directly contradicted . The Chinese ecological civilisation , Hamilton is forced to propose , only proves a deeper cynicism on the part of the Chinese government . Hilariously , he spends quite some time attacking the Chinese leadership for looking to its national history for philosophical grounding for the ecological civilisation - in this book that reduces all global thought to a battle between two German thinkers . <p> His interpretation is undone by his own description of China 's radical adoption of climate policies and development of a renewables industry after the failure of the Copenhagen COP . Yes , China now has the highest emissions @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ world on renewable and low carbon technology , including electric vehicles , batteries and solar panels . <p> He is , in the closing chapter , forced to admit that " Beijing understands that China is extremely vulnerable " to climate breakdown , is ruled by a Chinese Communist Party ( CCP ) " dominated by engineers and long term thinking " and has advanced plans for mitigation and adaptation , including strategic food stockpiles . The funniest and most revealing sentence is : " CCP leaders are obsessed with food security , understandably . " <p> MAGA <p> As well as foregrounding the apparent malevolence of the Chinese state , Hamilton is guilty of exaggerating the sometimes benevolence of the US state . The claim - which occasionally bubbles to the surface but is implied throughout - is that the Democratic governments of the US were serious about climate . <p> We then see how the United States has also been taken in by Schmitt 's schema . Hamilton is an economist and the more obvious choice would have been the battle of ideas between John Maynard Keynes , in the universalist corner - and Friedrich Hayek - in the self interest corner . Keynes and Hayek had a well documented influence on the think tanks behind climate policy and climate denial , respectively . But that story is well told . <p> The failure is - throughout - the reduction of complex geopolitics to a simple antinomy . Good versus evil . This is the " splitting ' brilliantly described by Melanie Klein 's psychoanalytic theory . The infantile mind divides the self , objects and experiences into extremes , the only-good and the only-bad . Schmitt based his entire philosophy on such a division . This flattening also means his interrogation of the COPs lacks a sociological grounding . The COP process itself is not designed to hold power , nor is it a neutral space or fair playing field . The COPs section of the book is a summary of the major events that contorts the facts to fit his schema @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ . The fact is Kant and Schmitt have more in common than most would like to admit . Both assumed that capitalism was the only way to run an economy , and therefore the only way we could run the planet . Kant argued that capitalism could be reformed , or contained . We could have capitalist states that cooperate when capitalism itself is under threat . Schmitt knew capitalism to be about war , exploitation , competition : a zero sum game . <p> But Hamilton 's approach " challenges economistic explanations that reduce the talks ' failure to the blocking power of the fossil fuel lobby . " He does , however , admit in his introduction that the Kant-Schmitt dualism excludes any real engagement with a third dead German philosopher , Karl Marx . <p> " Kant and Schmitt were concerned with states and did not pay much attention to the role of capital , " Hamilton observes . " Those who put fossil fuel corporations at the centre of the history of the climate struggle owe more to Marx 's political economy . " Later in @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ of this book 's story came brazenly into view at Dubai in 2023 ... fossil fuel power represented by the petrostates . " <p> Reintegrate <p> Marx obviously has not had a direct influence over elite thought - especially the elites that populate and dominate the COP conferences . But rather than this meaning Hamilton can completely ignore any Marxist analysis of state power and capitalism , this very ignorance could be understood as a significant part of the problem . <p> Marx argued that capitalism required an accumulation of wealth , and this very accumulation would necessarily result in increased extremes of social inequality . This social inequality in turn creates a world of ruthless competition , a propensity for conflict , and a justification of cruelty . It creates an economy where a few exhaust nature , while the many are seemingly powerless to prevent calamity . Marx made the point that none of this is inevitable . Through deliberate effort , it can be prevented . <p> Further , Marx desired the very thing that would stop the Schmittian nightmare becoming everyone 's lived reality : integration @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ that drove social inequality and turned people into two classes whose interests were directly opposed . The project was to reintegrate the human species , and indeed to reintegrate society and nature . Had this been achieved , Kant 's universalism could be more thoroughly universal - and climate breakdown would have been all but an impossibility . <p> Sabotaged <p> What Hamilton has shown us - and this is an invaluable insight - is that Kant / Keynes did not provide a philosophy that reveals and fundamentally challenges the logic of capitalism . As such , it can not explain the willingness of today 's global elites to allow climate breakdown to happen . It can not explain the propensity to war . So where does excluding Marx take us ? Hamilton concludes : " Perhaps the choice is no longer whether to be a Kantian or a Schmittian but whether to be a left Schmittian or a right Schmittian . " <p> Scylla is here the many-headed attempts to convince us that capitalism is the only possibility , and that capitalism can and must be reformed to avert @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ , and this is why the COPs proved to be pointless . Hamilton shows great courage in arguing that such a Scylla is a mere illusion and no longer holds any power over us . But he over-generalises to conclude that climate and environmental breakdown is " the decisive refutation of Kant 's belief in the progressive unfolding of reason and human moral development " . <p> But then Hamilton is immediately drawn into Charybdis , the whirlpool of doom and reaction . He ends the book imagining our near future " when Schmitt prevails " . Here climate breakdown is inevitable . Here fascism is inevitable . And here the worst instincts of humanity - the propensity to war and greed - are naturalised and normalised . " Schmitt 's dystopian outlook matches that of growing numbers who see the climate fight as lost . " <p> This defeatism is moral abdication . Despondency prevents Hamilton from learning the lesson hidden in plain sight in his own account of the climate struggle . We need to orient ourselves towards a clear and precise understanding of capitalism , the function @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ of both have sabotaged climate science , climate policy and the climate movement . Adshead is uncomfortable about how society talks about trauma . <p> We speak too casually about " trauma " . The term " trauma " , Adshead explains , ca n't be used to describe the painful events which occur in every human life : bereavement , unemployment , separation and interpersonal conflict . To call these events " traumatic " minimises the meaning of real trauma : surviving rape , abuse , disaster or attempted murder . <p> " Traumatic events , " she explains , " are those that cause intense fear and horror and are associated with the threat of death and serious injury or witnessing that in others . The problem now is that ' trauma ' has become shorthand for ' anything that upsets me ' and -- @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ which although very human is potentially unhelpful . " <p> It 's especially unhelpful , she says , when linked to the idea that being " upset " means someone " must be psychologically unwell " . <p> She questions whether we are now in the process of " the medicalisation of life 's ordinary suffering " . There is , she notes , " formal diagnostic criteria " in Britain for " distinguishing trauma from distressing events " . <p> This is what I 've learned from talking to a woman who has spent her life among killers and their victims : violence causes a " shattering " of the personality , both for the perpetrator and victim . <p> An act of violence shatters the self , whether it 's through pulling a trigger and by doing so destroying your own humanity and identity , or through surviving such an attack and living with the horrific notion that part of you has been stolen -- erased -- by the brutality of another . <p> Psychiatrist Dr Gwen Adshead ( Image : Richard Ansett , BBC ) <p> Childhood @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ perpetrators of trauma , the line between them is more blurred and complicated than one might think " . That 's five times what it is in the general population . " Childhood trauma is defined as experiences such as being beaten , sexually abused or neglected ; witnessing domestic violence ; or having parents who are addicts , or were imprisoned or mentally ill . <p> We tend to think of perpetrators as angry , and victims as sad , but that 's not always the case . @@137506170 <p> We have all now had the experience . A clip circulates online . The framing is plausible . It confirms what many people already suspect . Within hours , thousands of people are reacting to something they have not fully seen , from someone they have not fully heard , in a context they do not know . Then , much later , comes the qualification , the missing context , the longer recording , the correction that travels only a fraction as far as the original outrage . As Swift put it , " Falsehood flies , and the Truth comes limping after it . " <p> There is a lesson here , and it is not merely that everyone should be a little more careful online . We are entering a world in which seeing is no longer believing , hearing is no longer believing , and even a video clip must be treated as a kind of argument rather than straightforward evidence . It has been selected , framed , cut , captioned and served to us with a purpose . That purpose may be honest @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ the clip does not simply show us something , it wants us to react . <p> Some say that we are entering a post-truth age , but it may be more accurate to say that we are returning to the normal condition of mankind . For most of history , men did not live in a world of searchable archives , instant corrections , full transcripts and professionalised newsrooms . They lived amid rumour , gossip , partisan pamphlets , forged letters , official lies , unreliable messengers and stories that had acquired three new details by the time they reached the next village . <p> The difference now is not that falsehood exists . The difference is that falsehood can be manufactured instantly , dressed in the clothes of truth , and sent round the world before a sensible man has finished his breakfast . AI will make this worse , of course . The internet was already a machine for distributing half-truths ; AI gave it a factory . <p> Pope Leo XIV put the matter well when he warned journalists against the " ancient art of lying @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ civility against the quicksand of approximation and post-truth " . That phrase matters because it recognises both the novelty and the age of the problem . Pope Francis made precisely this point in his 2018 message on fake news . The first false report , he suggested , was the serpent 's temptation of Eve : not a crude denial , but a distortion , a malicious reframing , a use of partial truth against Truth itself . He wrote that " there is no such thing as harmless disinformation " . Catholics should take that seriously , because we are very good at noticing lies told by our enemies and rather less good at noticing lies that serve our side . <p> The doctored clip , the misleading headline , the out-of-context papal quotation , the fake statistic , the screenshot with no source : if it confirms our view of the world , we are inclined to be generous . We call it " basically true " . We say it " makes an important point " . We share it because the other side does worse . @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ truth , nor do we have permission to be careless because the error is convenient . A falsehood does not become pious because it embarrasses a liberal bishop , a progressive journalist , a secular politician or anyone else we dislike . It remains a falsehood . <p> There is , however , another temptation : the belief that the answer to all this is to become infinitely informed . To read more , follow more , watch more , verify more , refresh more , subscribe to more newsletters , keep 10 tabs open and treat every world event as a personal responsibility . This too is a trap . <p> There is something false about the modern piety of " staying informed " . In practice it often means surrendering the soul to a stream of distant provocations . A man reads about a war he does not understand , a court case he has not followed , a synod document he has not read , an American controversy he can not affect , a viral clip whose provenance he has not checked , and a scandal whose @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ not wiser , but more irritated . <p> The internet flatters us by making every event feel close . It puts Rome , Westminster , Washington , Gaza , X/Twitter , YouTube , TikTok and the parish WhatsApp group into the same nervous system . The result is not catholicity , but indigestion . We were not made to metabolise the whole world . <p> This is where the much-abused phrase ordo amoris is actually useful . It briefly escaped into American politics early last year when JD Vance invoked it and was promptly denounced for doing so . Whatever one thinks of his application , the underlying Christian instinct is sound enough : love must be ordered . We owe love to all men , but not in the same way , not with the same immediacy and not through the same duties . A man has obligations to his wife and children that he does not have to a stranger on the other side of the world , regardless of what Peter Singer says . He has duties to his parish , his household , his neighbours , @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ dissolved into a vague concern for mankind at large . <p> Charity begins with the person in front of you . Duty begins with the thing actually entrusted to you . The truth is not served by a man neglecting his wife , his children , his prayers , his work and his parish because he is busy forming strong opinions about matters he can not verify and can not influence . Of course this does not mean Catholics should become ignorant , incurious or parochial in the stupid sense . Some men must know more than others because their responsibilities require it . A journalist must investigate , a bishop must govern , a politician must deliberate , a father must know what threatens his household , a teacher must not be naive about the world into which his pupils are growing . But most of us should be far more honest about the difference between acquiring knowledge and engaging with agitprop . <p> Pope Leo 's recent defence of books is helpful here . Speaking to the Vatican Publishing House on 7 May , he said that the @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ that in the digital age the physical book reminds us of the need for thought , reflection and study . Reading , he said , " nourishes the mind " and forms a critical sense , guarding us against ideological shortcuts . <p> That is exactly the point . The opposite of online falsehood is not simply online fact-checking , necessary though that sometimes is . The deeper antidote is a mind trained to move more slowly , to weigh claims , to follow an argument , and to sit with reality rather than consume impressions of it . Books resist the nervous tempo of the feed . They do not flash , interrupt , notify , flatter or enrage . They ask for attention , and attention is one of the first casualties of the post-truth age . <p> A man who can not read a book will struggle to judge a headline . A mind formed by fragments will eventually mistake fragments for the whole . <p> There is an old Chinese image in the Tao Te Ching of the ideal life : to live in one 's @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ might faintly hear its chickens and dogs across the fields , and yet never feel the need to go there . One need not take Laozi as a political guide to see that there is wisdom in this image ; there is a peace in not making every distant noise one 's own business . <p> The Christian answer to post-truth is therefore not to become an amateur intelligence analyst , hunched over a screen , decoding every clip and chasing every rumour , but to recover the ordinary virtues that have been lost in the digital age : restraint , patience and the humility to admit that not every controversy requires our intervention . We should refuse convenient lies , avoid sharing what we have not checked , prefer the primary source to the viral summary , read more slowly , react less quickly , and be especially wary of anything that gives us the delicious pleasure of anger . Before we click , share or denounce , we might ask a simpler question : will knowing this help me discharge a duty , or will it merely give @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ catholic herald today <p> Our best content is exclusively available to our subscribers . @@137572367 <p> There appears to be an existing modern brand of madness in watching the world smolder while the people holding the matches tell you the air has never been clearer . For Genesis Owusu , the Ghanaian-Australian firebrand , this collective gaslighting was a source of passive anxiety and a catalyst for a total vocal exorcism . At 27 years old , arriving on the heels of two universally acclaimed , ARIA-sweeping records -- 2021 's Smiling with No Teeth and 2023 's Struggler -- Owusu could have comfortably settled into his hard-won status as alternative music 's most charismatic , genre-agnostic chameleon . Instead , he retreated to a renovated church in South Wales , staring down the barrel of global collapse . The result is his third full-length album , Redstar Wu &amp; The Worldwide Scourge , a 15-track manifesto that Owusu uses to operate under the heavy , sacred directive of Nina Simone , who famously declared that an artist 's ultimate duty is to reflect the times . And these are , undeniably , ugly times . Following an exhausting international touring schedule over the last @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ transatlantic rot : the resurgence of far-right extremism , the grotesque sanitisation of corporate greed , and the omnipresent , suffocating thrum of digital paranoia . This record is his furious response . It is an eclectic journey that maps the brutal intersection of social collapse and individual endurance , blending neo-soul , synth-punk , and Brit-rock into a cohesive sound of resistance . <p> Owusu does n't waste time on pleasantries . To prove that , the album kicks the door off its hinges with ' Pirate Radio ' , his first solo transmission in two years . Mounted on a heavy , rising , and intentionally distorted bassline , the track is jittery with the frantic energy of a man broadcasting from a subterranean bunker . " My life on Pirate Radio / You stand outside my stadium / One step outside your cranium / Mind been burnt by blue check mania , " he raps . It is a brilliant , brash skewering of tech-billionaire ego , an overt shot across the bow at the creation of our social media enclosures , delivered with a unique confidence @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ ... I 've been digging this grave for decades . I ca n't wait to use it , " it becomes the album 's undisputed statement of intent . <p> The cultural camouflage is off . This aggressive posture bleeds directly into the unrelenting following track ' Stampede ' . Channeling the raw , kinetic energy of classic indie rock and synth-punk , Owusu uses the track 's twitching synths and pounding drums to plant his flag firmly in the dirt . He is n't merely speaking truth to power ; he is actively attempting to organise a riot . " Giving my reply with a bat , find an oligarch get him taxed , " he barks , offering a fierce , blunt-force indictment of the wealth hoarding that plagues modern society . <p> This ferocious , anti-establishment streak continues on ' Big Dog ' , which takes direct aim at institutional powers , and the wildly ambitious ' Death Cult Zombie ' . The latter track is a fascinating musical pivot , utilising the rebellious swagger of 1980s Brit rock to dissect the terrifying normalisation of political extremism @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ is a visceral translation of the epidemic of hate Owusu witnessed on the road . The Welsh church where he and executive producer Dan Hulme recorded the album proved to be the perfect incubator for this defiance . Isolated from the sterile machinery of the music industry , the duo found the liberty to jam endlessly , allowing ideas to mutate organically without the pressure of a ticking studio clock . That unbounded approach is the secret engine of the album 's sonic vastness . <p> The political inferno reaches its absolute peak on the title track , ' The Worldwide Scourge ' . Here , the production shifts into a throbbing , ominous hip-hop tempo , anchored by ghostly chords and the militant , inevitable thump of marching snare drums . Owusu sounds less like a rapper and more like a battle-worn poet , lamenting the pillaging of Gaza and the violent erosion of basic human rights . Yet , amidst the grand geopolitical indictments , he possesses the sharp , observational eye to ground the " scourge in the quiet violence of everyday social etiquette . In a @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ the friction inherent in navigating public spaces in a Black body : " A white woman walked towards me and our eyes locked to meet / Felt the fear inside the air as she moved to cross the street / Should I blame her for seeing me and picturing a threat ? / Or the centuries of whipping that 's keeping women in debt . " It is a masterclass in songwriting , recognising how centuries of systemic prejudice filter down into the simple , devastating act of passing someone on the pavement . When the weight of this reality becomes unbearable , the natural human reflex is to simply shut down . Owusu anticipates this exhaustion . On the post-punk infused ' Human Again ' , he confronts the seductive , quiet slide into apathy . " Apathy is a grave , " he whispers over a simmering , melodic underscore , " do n't let the numbness drug you . " Remarkably , he pairs this grim warning with a magnetic , disco-style instrumental that physically demands movement . He executes a similar sleight of hand on the @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ forcing the listener to dance to the sound of societal decay , Owusu transforms the dancefloor into a sanctuary of collective survival . He understands that maintaining one 's capacity for movement and joy , a theme explored further on the alt-pop leaning ' Runnin Outta Time ' , is a radical act of resistance in a world designed to make you numb . <p> The duality of Redstar Wu is ultimately its greatest triumph . For all its fury and political fire , the album is intensely concerned with the endurance of love . Owusu pivots masterfully from defiance to deep introspection on ' Hellstar ' , a collaboration with American rapper Duckwrth . It is a dripping , deep-funk record masquerading as a post-apocalyptic love song . The premise is stunningly simple : the world is ending , so we might as well hold each other . " The world is burning , " Owusu croons over a chilling , undeniable summer groove , " come get a squeezing today . " This desperate , clinging warmth bleeds into ' Blessed Are the Meek ' , where elements @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ unbroken humanity , and the earnest ' Situations ' , which pleads for solidarity despite our endless ideological fractures. ' 4Life ' introduces melodic , wobbling and electronic rhythm . " I miss the life we used to live " , the calming lyrics breathe . <p> After an impressive display of sound bending , the compilation exhales with the tender , poetic closer , ' One 4 All ' . Stripped of the paranoid distortion and the marching snare drums , we are left with Owusu at his most entirely unguarded . " Wish you could look into the mirror , but that glass been chipped , " he confesses , tenderly unloading the burden of the past hour . " I think the world that I knew has changed a little bit . " It is a quiet admission of grief for the innocence we have collectively lost . <h> Referenced artists <p> But Genesis Owusu refuses to leave his listeners in the dark . He recognises that while the artist 's duty is to reflect the times , it is also to illuminate a way forward . @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ final , vital invocation , a spell against the encroaching dark : " It 's not forever , just for now , the sun will always set my child . But we gon na be alright . " <p> Redstar Wu &amp; The Worldwide Scourge is a magnificent achievement . By successfully joining the urgency of political protest with the aching vulnerability of the human heart , Genesis Owusu has crafted a bold state-of-the-day record . It is a profound document of this time , but its boundless musicality ensures it will far outlive the scourge it documents .

Now , reverse " the Oriental " and " the European " and you have an idea of the new Orientalism , where the enlightened East becomes the foil to a decadent , violent , barbaric West . <p> The new Orientalists are n't academics , policymakers or Wall Street Journal opinion columnists . @@137611793 <h> Is the declining birth rate a crisis ? <p> Experts are warning of trouble ahead as the annual number of babies being born in England and Wales plummets . With the consequences of falling birth rates already starting to hit , some have accused politicians of ignoring a looming " crisis " . <p> How many babies are being born ? According to newly published data from the Office for National Statistics , 585,396 babies were born last year , down from 594,677 in 2024 . The number of babies is at " the lowest level in almost half a century " , which " continues the long-term trend of falling births going back over the past decade " , said Greg Ceely , head of population health monitoring at the ONS . <p> Why are birth rates falling ? The trend is the result of a range of economic , social and cultural factors . The costs of housing and the instability of the housing market make starting a family seem riskier . The UK also has some of the highest childcare costs in Europe , relative to @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ opportunities for women , and broader shifts in gender roles and family dynamics . <p> Is this a crisis ? The latest data will " fuel political anxieties " about the " plummeting birth rate " , said The Times health editor Eleanor Hayward . A persistently low birth rate can create long-term demographic problems , since an ageing population means more retirees and fewer workers supporting pensions , healthcare , social care and taxes needed to fund public services . <p> Other consequences are " already being felt " , said The Guardian . Some schools are being forced to close , businesses such as soft-play centres and childminders are struggling , and midwifery courses are facing challenges because students must attend a minimum number of births .
